description:
A team workspace for running AI coding agents in parallel with isolated Git worktrees, live diff review, GitHub integration, and mobile access.

Lody is a team agent workspace: share coding agents with your team on phone and desktop. Shared sessions, live diffs, and one control plane keep your team and agents in sync.
Run agents in parallel with isolated Git worktrees and live diff review, use subscriptions you already have with Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Kimi, and any agent that speaks ACP, manage the same control plane in the terminal with CLI commands, and ship together in one workspace with shared sessions, usage by member, and PR, CI, and merge status in-session.
Version 0.109.0
✨ New Features
- Multi-repository projects: organize several Git repositories, submodules, and local folders into one project and work on cross-repository tasks in the same conversation. Add one in Settings → Projects, or right-click an existing project in the desktop sidebar. (On iOS, wait for the next mobile TestFlight build, or multi-repository conversations will not appear.)
- Per-repository PR views: in a multi-repository conversation, switch which repository is displayed to see its PRs, CI status, and actions; submodules are shown hierarchically.
- Magpie CLI import: import Magpie provider configuration through the CLI, so it can be used on machines without a desktop environment.
- Next prompt suggestions: Claude Code can now show the suggestion returned by the Agent in an empty composer; press Tab on desktop or tap “Apply” on mobile to fill it in.
- Local MCP sign-in: browser authorization, sign-out, and manual credential entry; credentials are stored in the local system credential store and are not synced with workspace configuration.
- Redesigned Schedules page: project and status filters, sorting, Settings and Run history views, and bulk cleanup of finished scheduled messages.
- Categorized task tabs: Subagents and background tasks now appear on separate tabs, making execution progress easier to follow.
- Cross-machine Role collaboration: when calling a remote Role from a local project, you can use a GitHub repository linked to the project and connected to the workspace; linked conversations stay nested in the list.
- iPhone Duo support: mobile layouts now follow the available screen space, improving folding, unfolding, and split-screen experiences.
- Scheduled messages: schedule messages, attachments, and references, then edit or cancel them; if the target machine is offline, the message is sent as a catch-up once the machine returns, within the validity window.
- Continue after a Claude quota reset: with one click, schedule continue to be sent after the quota resets, so the task can finish.
- DeepSeek Harness plugin management: manage provider plugins through the local CLI while keeping existing user configuration.
- Usage reset times: switch between a relative “resets in…” display and an absolute date and time in your local time zone.
- Larger remote file downloads: paid workspaces can download files up to 100 MiB; the CLI on the machine hosting the file must be updated as well.
🐛 Fixes & Improvements
- Fixed existing text sometimes being overwritten incorrectly when conversation content updates.
- Improved cross-repository PR linking and status sync, so status updates no longer affect existing PR links.
- Fixed machine online status in the sidebar flickering during brief reconnects.
- Fixed subscription usage information disappearing for some providers after adding a regular environment variable.
- DeepSeek conversations now collapse process output automatically after finishing, making the final reply easier to read.
- Improved mobile message queue action buttons, Role label alignment in the memory list, and icon display on the desktop sign-in page.
- Agents now prefer a new conversation when creating child conversations, unless a tab conversation is specified.
- Improved desktop sign-in recovery, avoiding unexpected sign-outs when network responses are slow at startup.
- Fixed the message queue sometimes failing to continue sending when sync order changed, and tasks that ended abnormally still showing as running.
- Creating a new conversation no longer waits for remote MCP defaults to sync; bulk conversation creation keeps the selected MCP.
- Fixed background tasks disappearing while running and executor information being lost after a Claude task completes.
- Kimi now shows the full plan before requesting plan approval.
- Fixed reasoning-effort options not matching model capabilities after switching models in Pi.
- Updated the Codex runtime with improved Skill list refresh, context compaction completion detection, and error messages after switching providers.
- Fixed multi-repository projects failing to start when submodule checkout is incomplete, and improved folder path display and sidebar archiving and collapse behavior.
- Fixed PR conflict-resolution actions not opening in the current conversation, and mobile renames incorrectly affecting other conversations.
- Fixed healthy Nowledge Mem connections being incorrectly reported as failing.
- Improved back-gesture conflicts on mobile machine management buttons, along with terminal tab, sign-in text, and home status display.
- When Claude hits its quota limit, you can schedule a continue message for after the reset directly from the prompt card; the scheduled time stays consistent with what the interface shows.
- When schedule send is unavailable, hover to see the specific reason.
- Improved the handoff between the interface and the keyboard when sending the first message on mobile; new conversations restore the last used project.
- The mobile message queue now uses a compact single-line layout.
- Improved link opening when several Lody versions are installed, handing conversation, new-conversation, and provider-import links to the running version.
- Improved alignment, color, and inline code styling for Agent prompt cards and reasoning content, reducing visual noise.
- Scheduled messages are easier to manage: the scheduled time appears next to the send button, scheduled messages are collected in the message queue, and you can change the time, edit the content, or cancel them directly.
- Improved message queue layout: a compact single-line display on phones and in narrow windows, with actions grouped in a “More” menu; finished one-time scheduled message records are kept for seven days and then cleaned up automatically.
- Fixed compatibility issues with composer prompt suggestions during onboarding.
- Fixed a message sent immediately after stopping a running task being cancelled as well; when stopping a task fails, the reason now appears in the conversation.
- When an Agent on the same machine sends a message to a running conversation over MCP, it can now steer the active task directly.
- Removed the extra execution-slot limit for scheduled tasks, so tasks wait on each other less.
- Newly created projects are selected automatically, and project groups can be edited directly from the project picker.
- Preparing project submodules now reuses local Git data, reducing repeated downloads.
- Fixed cookie passing in app previews, improving previews of pages that require sign-in.
- Fixed browser sign-in page errors and error handling for invalid invitation links.
- Fixed the mention menu not scrolling on mobile and incorrect message queue time formatting in Chinese.
- Improved wrapping and cursor display for prompt suggestions, temporarily hiding them while composing with an IME.
- Fixed scroll position jumping while reading in WebKit and improved the clarity of shared images.
- Improved file link detection and path copying, reducing incorrect jumps from relative paths.
- Clean up dedicated working directories for deleted conversations; archiving now removes only empty directories and keeps existing files.
- Fixed brief network delays causing online machines to be marked offline and conversation actions to be rejected.
- Improved recovery when scheduled tasks fail to load, preserving local edits and supporting manual retry.
- Fixed reasoning-effort options not matching the model list for some models, and the model and reasoning-effort settings being applied in the wrong order when Pi starts.
- Improved DeepSeek Harness startup compatibility, with a clear install prompt when a supported Node.js is missing.
- Fixed the notification button on the desktop window drag region not being clickable.
- Added support for macOS Emacs-style keybindings to move the cursor before and after file references in the composer.
Thanks to ktKongTong, scbizu, jijiamoer, and yayoinoyume for contributing to this release!
